statement: For max clique on graphs with N <= 1000, BBMC-style bitset coloring (independent-set extraction via bitset AND/complement) is dramatically faster than pairwise O(n^2) sequential greedy coloring, enabling the BnB to solve instances that otherwise timeout.
regime: Undirected graphs, N <= 1000, M <= 500000, 2-second time limit
mechanism: Pairwise coloring checks each vertex against all previously colored vertices (O(n^2) comparisons). BBMC coloring extracts independent sets using Q &= ~adj[v] which processes 64 vertices per word operation, reducing the constant factor by ~64x for MAXN=1001.
applicability_bounds: Applies when candidate sets are large (>100 vertices). For small candidate sets the overhead of bitset operations may not pay off vs simple array checks.

statement: Greedy clique construction with 5000 random restarts achieves ~92% of optimal on the test distribution, but BnB with BBMC coloring achieves 100%.
regime: Max clique problem #185 test distribution, N <= 1000
mechanism: Greedy restarts sample many random vertex orderings, finding cliques reachable by greedy extension. BnB exhaustively searches the space (pruned by coloring bounds), finding cliques that require non-greedy vertex selections.
applicability_bounds: The 92% figure is specific to this test distribution. On adversarial graphs (e.g., Keller graphs), greedy could perform much worse.
